sam_support: Customer acct=acme-corp reporting huge 99th tail on /embeddings route after our recent max_batch_size=64 change. 50th stayed ~30ms but 99th jumped to ~420ms. Happening when their clients mix tiny (1-2 tokens) and very large (2k tokens) embedding requests. Any quick ideas?

marta: Which route name + model? Also can you paste a minimal repro (sdk/curl) and any batching logs?

sam_support: Route: embeddings/768/standard, model=embed-v2. Sample python repro from the customer (they send a burst):

```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=...)
# sends mix of small and big
small = "hello"
big = "".join(["word "] * 2000)
for i in range(100):
    if i % 10 == 0:
        c.embeddings.create(model="embed-v2", input=big)
    else:
        c.embeddings.create(model="embed-v2", input=small)
# client config: batch_max_size=64, coalesce_window_ms=15
```

logs (from serving runtime):
```
[2026-03-17T12:01:05Z] req=abc123 size=1 waiting_for_batch queue_pos=3
[2026-03-17T12:01:05Z] req=def456 size=2048 triggered_flush reason=batch_full
[2026-03-17T12:01:05Z] req=abc123 served latency=412ms
[2026-03-17T12:01:06Z] req=ghi789 size=1 waiting_for_batch queue_pos=7
[2026-03-17T12:01:06Z] req=ghi789 served latency=398ms
```

runtime_dan: That pattern looks like mixed-size starvation. Large request arrives and the batch waits for it or for window to expire; with max_batch_size large, the big request causes many small requests to be coercively batched and delayed. Our dynbatch currently doesn't preempt or evict a big request mid-assembly. Do you have shard queue stats? Endpoint /internal/queue_stats can show small-vs-large wait distribution.

sam_support: Pulled stats (last 5m):
```
queue_backlog.small.count=320
queue_backlog.large.count=18
wait_p50.small=22ms
wait_p99.small=1100ms
wait_p50.large=180ms
```
so the 99th for smalls spikes when a large lands.

sre_jen: Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size on that route to 8 or 16; 2) enable small-request preemption (route config flag: "preempt_small_requests": true); 3) lower coalesce_window_ms to 5ms for that customer. You can patch via the admin API: 

curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/routes/embeddings/768/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>' -d '{"max_batch_size":8,"preempt_small_requests":true,"coalesce_window_ms":5}'

That should reduce the tail quickly (tradeoff: small drop in aggregate throughput).

ml_ops_ryan: Longer term: add size-based priority tagging in the routing policy (requests < 64 tokens get high priority), or separate capacity pools for small/large embeddings. Also consider dynamic coalesce heuristics: increase window when request sizes uniform, shrink when variance high. Finally encourage SDK to expose per-request priority or size hint so the router can schedule earlier.

sam_support: Applied max_batch_size=8 + preempt_small_requests=true for acct=acme-corp (rolled 12:03 UTC). Customer ran a quick test: 99th dropped from ~420ms -> ~45ms, p50 unchanged. Throughput impact negligible (approx -1.8% qps). Customer confirmed fixes their visible latency complaint. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: config-rollout embeddings/768 v2026-03-17-2 started by marta — targeting 3 shards, rolling update.

marta: Can we create a KB for "mixed-size embedding tail latency" with repro steps + recommended mitigations? Please add the console commands and the curl snippets.

sam_support: Will open support ticket + KB, and recommend default route change for high variance customers. Closing the thread once KB is up.

sre_jen: Nice quick mitigation. Follow-up: add telemetry alert for p99_small > 200ms when coalesce_window_ms < 20ms. :white_check_mark:
